title: Protecting people affected by HIV and AIDS

blocks.heading: Protecting people affected by HIV and AIDS
blocks.text: Government can support non-discrimination, confidential handling of relevant personal information, accurate workplace education and access to prevention, care and support. Protection should respond to actual capability and workplace needs rather than assumptions about perceived HIV status. The [ILO workplace principles](https://www.ilo.org/publications/ilo-code-practice-hivaids-and-world-work) emphasise non-discrimination, confidentiality and care. A policy needs accessible complaints and implementation, not simply a statement on a wall. Education can challenge stigma but may not by itself stop unfair decisions; oversight and fair processes also matter. This explains general protection approaches and does not prescribe medical treatment or determine an individual legal claim.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: At fictional Tula Print, a capable worker is excluded from ordinary opportunities because colleagues speculate about HIV status. Management considers an education session alone or a fair-treatment policy with confidential reporting and action. Education can correct misinformation, but the stated exclusion also needs a response to conduct and decisions. Prefer education combined with enforceable workplace standards, confidential reporting and fair access to opportunities. Avoid requiring public disclosure as a condition of respect; assess the job and actual needs instead of rumours.
